intent: Eight individual adjective tasks teach contextual meaning, degree, modification, comparison and bounded time claims.

transfer.stem: Which reading keeps the words in their actual context?
transfer.passage:
A better display for our visit
Our class was making a display about a visit to a country park. A good map made our long walk easier, although it did not make the path any shorter. An old map also showed a path across a field, but we had not checked whether that path was still open.
For the display, we tried to make a small landscape model. The sand was too fine to hold the shape we wanted. We changed our materials, and the next model was a great improvement on the first one. It still needed clearer labels. A new shelf gave us more space to store our work.
At lunchtime, it was nice to eat outside for a change. A bad smell came from a blocked drain nearby, so we chose a different table. On our way back, a park worker showed us a young bird that had not learned to fly. She explained that it was still growing; nobody said it would never fly.

options.text: The old map did not verify today’s access; the sand had small grains; the bird had not learned to fly at that time.
The old map confirmed the path was safe today; the sand had small grains; the bird had not learned to fly at that time.
The old map did not verify today’s access; fine meant sunny weather; the bird had not learned to fly at that time.
The old map did not verify today’s access; the sand had small grains; the bird could never fly in its whole life.

answer.display: The old map did not verify today’s access; the sand had small grains; the bird had not learned to fly at that time.
